|book= E |publisher= |page= 116 {{Exp Game|TLoZ, ALttP, OoT, OoT3D, MM, MM3D, TWW, TWWHD, TMC, TP, TPHD, PH, ST, SS}}}}{{Cite Guide|LA Nintendo|page= 10}}{{Cite|{{Big|Arrow}}

A common arrow. Its shaft was carved from the wood of a sturdy tree.|Inventory|TotK}} They are sharp projectiles that are shot with a [[Bow]]. Many varieties of Arrows exist throughout the ''Zelda'' series, including [[Silver Arrow]]s, [[Fire Arrow]]s, [[Ice Arrow]]s, [[Light Arrow]]s, [[Bomb Arrow]]s, [[Shock Arrow]]s, and [[Ancient Arrow]]s. ==Location and Uses== ==={{TLoZ|-}}=== {{Descriptions TLoZ}} Arrows can be shot using the Bow in {{TLoZ}}.{{Cite Manual|quote= Link can use them only if he has both the bow and an arrow.|game= TLoZ|page= 24}} [[Link]] cannot fire Arrows until he has purchased the Arrow from a [[Merchant]]. After Link has done so, he will be able to shoot Arrows by consuming one [[Rupee]] per shot.{{Cite Manual|quote= For each arrow Link shoots, he loses one ruby.|game= TLoZ|page= 24}} Arrows deal 2 damage to enemies that can be inflicted by them. [[Pols Voice]]s are weak to Arrows and will be defeated by them in one hit. [[Gohma]]s can only be defeated with Arrows.{{Cite Manual|quote= Oh, by the way, there are some enemies that can be disposed of using only the bow and arrow. So be alert!|game= TLoZ|page= 24}} [[Silver Arrow]]s also appear in the game, which deal 4 damage to enemies and must be used as the final blow on [[Ganon]] to destroy him. ==={{ALttP|-}}=== Arrows appear in {{ALttP}} and can be shot using the Bow. Link can purchase Arrows at [[Shop]]s, acquire them from defeated enemies, or obtain them from [[Treasure Chest]]s. Link can increase the amount of Arrows he can carry by spending Rupees at the [[Pond of Happiness]]. Silver Arrows also return and must be used to defeat Ganon. ==={{LA|-}}=== Arrows appear in {{LA}} and are shot by using the [[Bow]]. If Link equips [[Bomb]]s at the same time as the Bow, he can fire the Bombs with Arrows.{{Cite Guide|LA Nintendo|page= 105}} Link can acquire Arrows by defeating [[Enemy|Enemies]] or purchasing 10 of them from the [[Town Tool Shop]] in [[Mabe Village]] for 10 [[Rupee]]s. ==={{OoT|-}}=== In {{OoT}}, Arrows are shot using the [[Fairy Bow]], which can only be used while Link is an adult. Link can purchase Arrows from Shops or [[Business Scrub]]s if he has the Bow.{{Cite|Knock it off! Leave me alone, and I will sell you Arrows! 30 pieces 70 Rupees they are!|Business Scrub|OoT}}{{Cite|You can buy arrows at a shop only if you have a bow. Have you got one, mister?|Fado (Ocarina of Time)|OoT}} Arrows can also be found by cutting grass, defeating enemies, or within small Treasure Chests. Link can carry more Arrows by buying larger [[Quiver]]s.{{Cite|You upgraded your quiver to a {{Color OoT3D|Red|Big Quiver}}! Now you can carry more arrows—{{Color OoT3D|Yellow|40}} in total!|N/A|OoT3D}} Link can shoot Arrows while riding [[Epona]] and can shoot Arrows through the [[Fire]] of lit [[Torch]]es to light other Torches or melt ice. [[Fire Arrow]]s, [[Ice Arrow]]s, and [[Light Arrow]]s appear for the first time in {{OoT|-}}. Light Arrows are needed to defeat [[Ganondorf]]. ==={{MM|-}}=== In {{MM}}, Arrows are shot with the [[Hero's Bow]], which is the main item of the [[Woodfall Temple]]. Link can purchase Arrows from Shops, find them by cutting [[Grass]], or acquire them from defeated [[Enemy|Enemies]]. Link can shoot Arrows while riding on Epona and can shoot them through the Fire of lit Torches to light other Torches. Fire Arrows, Ice Arrows, and Light Arrows return as central [[Dungeon]] [[Item]]s. Link can carry 30 Arrows at first, and can increase his carrying capacity by earning new [[Quiver]]s at the [[Town Shooting Gallery|Town]] and [[Swamp Shooting Gallery|Swamp Shooting Galleries]]. ==={{FS|-}}=== In {{FS}}, the [[Links]] do not collect Arrows, but can shoot them with the various Bows found throughout the game. ==={{TWW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= TWW |type= Characters |category= Items in The Wind Waker |needs= Detailed information on the following: * Where they are found * How much they cost * What they do }} Arrows are shot in {{TWW}} with the use of the Hero's Bow. Arrows can be purchased from Shops, found by cutting grass, or acquired from defeated enemies. Link can shoot Arrows while sailing the [[Great Sea]] on the [[King of Red Lions]]. Light Arrows also appear in {{TWW|-}} as a crucial weapon against Ganondorf. Link can initially carry 60 Arrows, but can acquire an expanded Quiver at [[Thorned Fairy Island]]. ==={{FSA|-}}=== In {{FSA}}, the Links shoot Arrows from the various Bows found throughout Hyrule. ==={{TMC|-}}=== Arrows can be shot in {{TMC}} by using the Bow. Arrows can be purchased from Shops, found by cutting [[Grass]], or acquired from defeated [[Enemy|Enemies]]. Link also obtain Light Arrows from [[Gregal]] after saving him from an evil spirit. Link can initially carry 50 Arrows but can earn and purchase upgraded [[Quiver]]s. ==={{TP|-}}=== {{TP Item Properties/Store |type = Arrow }} In {{TP}}, Arrows are shot with the Hero's Bow. Link can purchase Arrows at Shops, find them by cutting grass, or acquire them from defeated enemies. Link can also pick up Arrows that land on the ground when enemies miss their mark. Like in {{OoT|-}} and {{MM|-}}, Link can shoot Arrows while riding Epona. He can expand his capacity of Arrows by beating the [[STAR Game]] in [[Hyrule Castle Town]], acquiring bigger Quivers from [[Purlo]] as rewards. [[Bomb Arrow]]s appear for the first time in {{TP|-}} and can be used to destroy rocks and inflict high amounts of damage to Enemies. ==={{PH|-}}=== In {{PH}}, Link can shoot Arrows with the Bow. Upon first earning the Bow in the [[Temple of Courage]], Link can initially carry 20 Arrows. He can increase his carrying capacity by acquiring new [[Quiver]]s. ==={{ST|-}}=== In {{ST}}, Link can fire Arrows by using the Bow. Link can acquire Arrows at Shops or by defeating [[Enemy|Enemies]]. Link can carry 20 Arrows upon first earning the Bow. He can increase his carrying capacity by acquiring new [[Quiver]]s. ==={{SS|-}}=== Arrows can be shot with a Bow in {{SS}}. They can be purchased at the [[Gear Shop]] in the [[Skyloft Bazaar]]. Additionally, if enemies fire Arrows at Link and they hit the ground, he can pick them up. Link can increase the amount of Arrows he can carry by equipping a Quiver to his [[Adventure Pouch]]. ==={{ALBW|-}}=== In {{ALBW}}, Link does not collect Arrows, but can still shoot them with a Bow. Like all items in the game, Link uses up his [[Energy Gauge]] to fire Arrows. ==={{TFH|-}}=== In {{TFH}}, the Links shoot Arrows from Bows that can be found in various [[Levels in Tri Force Heroes|Level]]s. Firing them uses up their Energy Gauges. ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{BotW Item Properties/Store |type = Arrow |strength = |durability = |flammable = |magnetic = |buoyant = |conductive = |guardian = |throw = |throw effect = }} {{Compendium/Extract|Arrow}} In {{BotW}}, Arrows are commonly found and are made from sturdy [[Tree]]s. They can also be found as bundles.{{Cite|{{Big|Arrow x5}}
A bundle of five common arrows.
The shafts of these arrows were carved from the wood of a sturdy tree.|N/A|BotW}}{{Cite|{{Big|Arrow x10}}
A bundle of 10 common arrows.
The shafts of these arrows were carved from the wood of a sturdy tree.|N/A|BotW}} They can be used to strike [[Enemy|Enemies]] from afar with any [[Bow]], except for the [[Twilight Bow]] and [[Bow of Light]], which only shoot [[Light Arrow]]s. Shooting an Enemy in the head with an Arrow will inflict double damage.{{Cite|{{Big|Critical Hits}}
Hitting a monster or enemy in the head with an arrow deals double the normal amount of damage.|Tips and Tricks|BotW}} If an Enemy is scouting on a lookout post, Link can shoot them in the head to instantly defeat them.{{Fact}} Link can shoot Arrows while riding a [[Horse]] and from atop the [[Master Cycle Zero]]. Arrows will penetrate and stick to certain [[Object]]s, such as wood, and certain [[Material]]s, such as [[Hylian Shroom]]s.{{Which}} Arrows can also be lit on fire and used to spread Fire to flammable Objects, such as grass, wood, and [[Torch]]es. Arrows can be purchased from the following locations: * The [[Arrow Specialty Shop]] in [[Gerudo Town]] * The [[Coral Reef]] in [[Zora's Domain]] * The [[East Wind]] in [[Hateno Village]] * The [[General Shoppe]] in [[Korok Forest]] * [[The Slippery Falcon]] in [[Rito Village]] * The [[Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch)]] * [[The Curious Quiver]] in [[Kakariko Village]] * [[Shaillu]]'s Arrow Shop in [[Kara Kara Bazaar]] * The Fish market in [[Lurelin Village]] * [[Botrick]] at [[Outskirt Stable]] * [[Beedle]] everywhere he appears * [[Gartan]] in the [[Gerudo Desert]] and at the [[Gerudo Canyon Stable]] * [[Giro]] in the forest near the [[Dueling Peaks]] * [[Jini]] at the [[Mounted Archery Camp]] Link can find Arrows hidden in [[Treasure Chest]]s throughout Hyrule Kingdom or as enemy drops. [[Bokoblin]]s, [[Moblin]]s, [[Lizalfos]], and [[Lynel]]s are capable of using Bows and sometimes use Arrows. Link can also pick up Arrows that enemies fire at the ground after missing their shot. Link can stun [[Guardian]]s by shooting them in the eye with Arrows. Fire Arrows, Ice Arrows, Light Arrows, and Bomb Arrows return in {{BotW|-}}, and [[Shock Arrow]]s and [[Ancient Arrow]]s make their first appearance. Arrows are one of the required Items for crafting [[Ancient Arrow]]s by using the [[Ancient Oven]], [[Cherry|Ancient Oven]], at the [[Akkala Ancient Tech Lab]]. ==={{TotK|-}}=== {{Compendium/Extract/TotK|Arrow}} {{Stub|TotK}} {{TotK Item Properties/Store |type = Arrow |strength = |durability = |flammable = |magnetic = |buoyant = |conductive = }} {{Frameless|[[File:TotK Arrow Menu Icon.png|thumb|right|100px|alt= An icon of an Arrow.|An Arrow icon from {{TotK|-}}]]}} Only regular Arrows appear in {{TotK}}. They can be found as bundles.{{Cite|{{Big|Arrow x10}}
A bundle of 10 common arrows.
The shafts of these arrows were carved from the wood of a sturdy tree.|N/A|TotK}} By [[Fuse|Fusing]] Arrows with [[Material]]s, [[Link]] is able to modify his Arrows and change their properties. ==={{EoW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= EoW |type= Items |category= Items in Echoes of Wisdom |needs= Detailed information on the following: * Who uses Arrows * If there is an Arrow capacity for Link * Where Arrows can be found and bought }} {{Stub|EoW}} [[Link]] and [[Zelda]] both use Arrows with the [[Bow of Might]]. These Arrows are capable of damaging black webbing and magical [[Crystal]]s. Zelda does not collect Arrows and can only use them in [[Swordfighter Form]], which expends her [[Energy]]. ==Other Appearances== ==={{AST|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|AST}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{TLoZ|-}} (TV Series)=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{ZA|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|ZA}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SSBM|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|SSBM}} Link uses a bow to fire arrows in the Smash Bros. series. In this series, all depictions of link have an unlimited supply of arrows. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SCII|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|SCII}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SSBB|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|SSBB}} Multiple portrayals of Link use a Bow to fire Arrows in {{SSBB}}. All depictions of Link have an unlimited supply of Arrows. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{HW|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Arrows are obtained alongside the [[Bow]] in "[[The Sorceress of the Woods]]" [[Scenario]] in {{HW}}. The Bow can be used by all [[Warrior]]s, and there is no limit to the number of Arrows that can be fired. Arrows can be upgraded to the [[Light Arrow]]s.{{How}} Zant uses 8-bit Arrows as his 8-bit Weapons.{{Which}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SSB4|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|SSBfN3DS, SSBfWU}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SSBU|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Arrows are shot from [[Link]]'s [[Traveler's Bow]] in {{SSBU}}. Arrows that don't make contact with any Fighters will stick into surfaces. They can then be picked up and thrown. If they are retrieved by Link, he can fire two Arrows at once by using the previous Arrow in tandem with a new Arrow. [[Young Link]] and [[Toon Link]] also use Arrows as part of their movesets. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{CoH|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|CoH}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|AoC}} Link fires a volley of arrows as his special move for his One-Handed Weapons moveset.
